ownership: Original Design Taste teaching and geometric artwork. Contemporary interpretations, not named historical replicas; cited institutional pages are outbound context only.

lessons.title: Observe relationships
lessons.concept: Separate visible line, shape, value, space and emphasis from interpretation.
lessons.task: Annotate the unchanged original in five regions. Predict attention, retain three same-element layouts, revise spacing or scale and inspect 600 and 150 views.
lessons.formats: Unchanged-reference analysis SVG; three 600x600 SVG/PNG compositions; 150x150 SVG/PNG inspections; portable evidence JSON.
lessons.limitations: Evidence presence is not mastery or audience response.

lessons.title: Color lives in context
lessons.concept: A contextual appearance is not a changed numerical RGB value.
lessons.task: Predict, compare six equal-size surrounds around invariant RGB 128,128,128, revise one background and report difference or no difference.
lessons.formats: Six 600x600 SVG/PNG pairs; before/revised values and profile note in JSON.
lessons.limitations: Uncalibrated browser RGB is not print-profile proof.

lessons.title: Type carries exact content
lessons.concept: Nominal type size does not establish glyph coverage or optical spacing.
lessons.task: Edit exact title and supporting text on three typography-only posters. Predict reading order, compare at 1200x1600 and 300x400, change tracking or leading only, retain glyph/fallback journal.
lessons.formats: Three editable 1200x1600 SVG posters and full/300x400 PNG/SVG views; font inventory and process Markdown; JSON.
lessons.limitations: Only system fonts; no bundled font binaries. Unfamiliar scripts require qualified review; rendering is not reader testing.

lessons.title: Claims have locators
lessons.concept: A school, movement, tradition and technique are different categories. Citation is not rights clearance.
lessons.task: Inspect two outbound sources, fill source ID/page/passage locator/access date/limits, compare context and revise an overgeneralized claim. Propose original contemporary work, not a historical replica.
lessons.formats: Two editable research cards and before/after Markdown; portable JSON.
lessons.limitations: Learner cards remain learner-unreviewed. Imported source status is unchanged; inaccessible passages stay unverified.

lessons.title: Edges make relationships
lessons.concept: Collage and photorealism have different edge/lighting criteria.
lessons.task: Edit original vector layers on a cover; predict a mask or scale change, compare before and revised, inspect full and 300x400 views and explain edge intent.
lessons.formats: 1200x1600 editable layered SVG; full/300x400 SVG/PNG before/revised; asset inventory and JSON.
lessons.limitations: Original vectors only; no photo imports. SVG layers are not PSD proof. Native Photoshop blocked by owner decision.

lessons.title: A system, not just a mark
lessons.concept: Constants and controlled variants must survive declared use conditions.
lessons.task: Compare three distinct original constructions, make a provisional selection, edit mark/wordmark spacing, test actual 32 and 256 mark uses and one-color/reverse, retain optical revision and rejection rationale.
lessons.formats: Three editable concept SVGs; selected mark/wordmark; 32/256 SVG/PNG specimens; BRAND.md; JSON.
lessons.limitations: 32px is a mark-only use, not a promise that full wordmark reads at 32px. Trademark/cultural/legal clearance and human selection remain pending.

lessons.title: One message, six formats
lessons.concept: Adapt hierarchy rather than stretching artwork.
lessons.task: Edit exact event/title/date/place across a poster, flyer and four social cards. Compare shortest/longest fixtures, revise title spacing and recheck all affected formats at the same size.
lessons.formats: 1200x1600 poster, 600x800 flyer, four 1080x1080 editable SVG/PNG cards; stress fixtures; JSON.
lessons.limitations: Original fictional event; no attendee, client or reader response inferred.

lessons.title: Reading order has continuity
lessons.concept: Page styles can be constants while cover metaphors differ.
lessons.task: Compare three cover directions, choose provisionally, edit eight original pages, inspect full and reduced outputs, revise a page/cover and explain reading order and rejected alternatives.
lessons.formats: Eight 1200x1600 page SVGs and full/300x400 PNG/SVG; three cover SVGs; printable inert publication HTML; JSON.
lessons.limitations: Digital publication only; no press-ready, bleed/profile, native InDesign or human approval claim.

lessons.title: A hold has a purpose
lessons.concept: Movement must explain something the static sequence cannot.
lessons.task: Edit six 1920x1080 storyboards and shot purpose/copy/holds. Predict pacing, play/pause/scrub an eight-second 24fps browser animatic, revise one hold and compare before/after timing. Keep static sequence.
lessons.formats: Six SVG/PNG frames; browser playback; editable project JSON; timing JSON/CSV and static HTML.
lessons.limitations: Browser animatic and source/frame artifacts are not an encoded MP4. Export capability must be reported separately.

lessons.title: Identity over time
lessons.concept: Position, scale and type can vary without losing declared constants.
lessons.task: Edit original mark/wordmark keyframes, holds and timing. Play/pause/scrub a ten-second 1920x1080 24fps identity source; compare one timing revision in before/revised playback and retain first/mid/final frames.
lessons.formats: Browser motion playback; editable JSON; first/mid/final SVG/PNG; timing and brand Markdown; static HTML.
lessons.limitations: Native operation is blocked/unrun. Source/frames do not certify encoded video or audience identification.

lessons.title: Cuts, sound, captions
lessons.concept: Caption timing, safe regions and audio relationships need actual playback, not a recipe claim.
lessons.task: Edit six original five-second narrative shots, captions/SRT times, sound frequencies/gain and cut holds. Play/pause/scrub thirty seconds, compare a cut/caption/audio revision and inspect peaks and timing. Original synthesized tones are not speech.
lessons.formats: 1920x1080 24fps browser edit; JSON; frames; UTF-8 SRT; original PCM WAV; timing/peaks JSON; static HTML.
lessons.limitations: Canonical caption-to-actual-speech alignment is blocked: no recorded speech. Encoded video is not produced unless actual capability succeeds. These exact gates remain failed, not 11 complete.

lessons.title: A claim resolves to evidence
lessons.concept: Authorship, actual revisions, source support and acceptance are distinct.
lessons.task: Import a validated original production project from 05/06/08/10/11; retain its alternatives/before/after and required-size exports. Link each case-study decision to artifact/criterion, revise an unsupported claim and export separate gates.
lessons.formats: Markdown case study and support ledger; selected editable SVG/JSON; inherited required-size flat views and before/after; gate JSON.
lessons.limitations: No self-awarded independent PASS, learner mastery or aesthetic acceptance. Missing production/native/video/human gates stay explicit.

movements.title: Material and making
movements.teaching: Compare an original hand-like repeated leaf unit with a typography-only communication field. Change repeat spacing and stroke weight: does material rhythm help this fictional workshop message? Make the process visible rather than treating a botanical motif as the whole movement.
movements.limits: Digital strokes do not model hand craft, labor, industrial production or object use. This is original interpretation, not a Morris reproduction. S24 retains its canonical unreviewed status.

regions.label: Repeated handmade unit
regions.explanation: Unequal paired strokes form a self-authored leaf. Count controls repetitions, not a historical motif.

regions.label: Workshop message
regions.explanation: Calm original type stays independent of ornament; compare the typography-only state.

regions.label: Unit/field interval
regions.explanation: The white interval separates the making rhythm from information. Repetition is a material proposal, not source history.

movements.title: A shared line system
movements.teaching: Vary the bow of a self-authored stem and the contour width. Compare how an image contour and a headline field share a surface; retain three contour abstractions without tracing a plant photograph.
movements.limits: A curve is not the whole international movement; geometric examples and varied regional contexts are not modeled. No named artist replica. See unreviewed S25.

regions.label: Continuous contour
regions.explanation: A cubic stem bends by the declared bow value; changing it alters negative space, not just color.

regions.label: Headline field
regions.explanation: The exact phrase is actual system-font text, not an imported lettering specimen.

regions.label: Contour enclosure
regions.explanation: Original leaf ellipses share the stem rhythm but do not identify every Art Nouveau work.

movements.title: Stepped rhythm
movements.teaching: Edit step count and width in an original stepped construction. Compare monochrome versus color while keeping form; test symmetry, linear rhythm and a calm information base. Gold and black are not requirements.
movements.limits: Materials, historical-modern combinations and colonial context exceed this digital diagram. No exotic borrowed motifs or named-work copy. S26 remains unreviewed.

regions.label: Stepped silhouette
regions.explanation: Centered tiers contract upward; two independent dimensions govern rhythm.

regions.label: Information base
regions.explanation: The original announcement remains outside the stepped silhouette.

regions.label: Symmetry axis
regions.explanation: An explicit centerline lets you test symmetry without claiming it is universal.

movements.title: Asymmetrical plane intervals
movements.teaching: Change the partition and boundary weight of an original orthogonal color-field proposal. Compare unequal areas and remove color to test hierarchy. This complements the preserved pilot plane reconstruction, not a familiar painting copy.
movements.limits: Publication, architecture and social aims are not modeled; color recipe is not the whole movement. Actual S28 status is unchanged.

regions.label: Unequal color fields
regions.explanation: A variable vertical partition changes the two areas and their boundary.

regions.label: Retained original identity
regions.explanation: The small original label anchors this diagram to our teaching project, not a historical painting.

regions.label: Orthogonal crossing
regions.explanation: Horizontal and vertical strokes cross without decorative diagonals; test interval relationships.

movements.title: Direction for a public message
movements.teaching: Change the direction band and information-block scale for an original public-interest message. Explain the communication purpose of each hierarchy; a red diagonal alone is not historical Constructivism.
movements.limits: Political context, production and social function remain larger than this display. Contemporary proposal only; S29 is unreviewed, no invented political endorsement.

regions.label: Directional band
regions.explanation: The band rotates around its center, suggesting a proposed reading direction.

regions.label: Primary message block
regions.explanation: Actual exact copy stays level rather than becoming unreadable decoration.

regions.label: Production note
regions.explanation: A secondary block asks who the message serves; direction is not a social-purpose proof.

movements.title: Tension without representation
movements.teaching: Move and rotate three original geometric forms. Predict the weight of their intervals, retain six balance states and explain why this nonrepresentational study is different from a communication-engineering proposal.
movements.limits: Not a Malevich reconstruction or a universal formula; original formal study only. Historical aims and S30 review are separate from Constructivism.

regions.label: Rotated plane
regions.explanation: The square has no depicted object; rotation changes its tension with the field.

regions.label: Circular counterweight
regions.explanation: The circle radius is independently controlled. Formal contrast is not a historical aim by itself.

regions.label: Bar interval
regions.explanation: A third bar makes the empty gap measurable rather than filling every region.

movements.title: Chance against a claim
movements.teaching: Record a deterministic seed and compare planned versus chance placement of original fragments. Edit the critical phrase and explain the cultural question; randomness alone does not establish Dada.
movements.limits: Original fragments only; no newspaper scans, historical slogans or copied art. Antiwar/social critique belongs in sourced context, not a randomness success claim. S31 remains unreviewed.

regions.label: Chance fragments
regions.explanation: An integer seed reproduces original rectangles and a cut form; no external asset enters the collage.

regions.label: Critical phrase
regions.explanation: Exact editable words supply a question; the chance rule cannot supply its meaning.

regions.label: Planned/chance baseline
regions.explanation: Switch off chance and compare the same fragments before making a claim about disruption.

movements.title: An unexpected relationship
movements.teaching: Write a short encounter, then change an original vessel's relative scale and lift beside an arch. Explain the uncanny relationship while retaining an independent headline. Flying objects alone are not the movement.
movements.limits: No named artwork replica, dream diagnosis or universal method. Unconscious/liberation context remains sourced and unreviewed at S32.

regions.label: Altered vessel scale
regions.explanation: The original cup changes relative size, creating a proposed conceptual encounter.

regions.label: Encounter phrase
regions.explanation: The words make your premise inspectable; interpretation is not a diagnosis.

regions.label: Arch relationship
regions.explanation: A stable original arch acts as the comparison anchor for scale and lift.

movements.title: The page is an open field
movements.teaching: Transcribe the exact announcement and glyphs. Compare centered and asymmetrical information order by changing alignment, title size and leading. No imported font; asymmetry never excuses clipping or illegibility.
movements.limits: Contemporary original system-font proposal, not a historical poster. Actual readership and S33 passage review remain separate.

regions.label: Alignment rule
regions.explanation: A visible rule gives the text blocks a spatial anchor; alignment is a controlled decision.

regions.label: Actual title glyphs
regions.explanation: Title lines are editable text, not an image or language-neutral pattern.

regions.label: Date/place hierarchy
regions.explanation: Supporting facts stay readable in their own block; compare retrieval rather than assuming a neutral style.

movements.title: An ordinary object, several narratives
movements.teaching: Repeat a self-authored cup across original panels. Change panel count and narrative label; compare repetition with one object, and explain whether the sequence means more than a palette change.
movements.limits: No branded packaging, characters or named artist replication. Popular/commercial culture context at S35 is unreviewed; no universal Pop recipe.

regions.label: Repeated ordinary cup
regions.explanation: The repeated unit is our original object, not a commercial package.

regions.label: Narrative labels
regions.explanation: Editable words change the interpretation; palette alone cannot establish critique.

regions.label: Panel sequence
regions.explanation: Distinct framed intervals let you compare count and order without flashing.

movements.title: Static spacing, not flashing
movements.teaching: Discomfort warning: stop viewing if uncomfortable. Vary static stripe pitch and width, one variable at a time; retain six comparisons. Readable information stays outside the optical field. Nothing autoplays or flashes.
movements.limits: No measured perceptual response, animation or historical replica. Static patterns can still cause discomfort; quiet alternative is always available. S36 remains unreviewed.

regions.label: Static stripe field
regions.explanation: Separated lines repeat without temporal modulation; no flashing is generated.

regions.label: Independent information
regions.explanation: The instruction remains outside optical tension and warns about discomfort.

regions.label: Spacing boundary
regions.explanation: The field is spatially bounded; compare pitch while holding width constant.

movements.title: Reduction and object presence
movements.teaching: Reduce an original object arrangement through three stages, then change interval and object count. Record when identification or meaning is lost. This screen study cannot demonstrate material or physical presence.
movements.limits: Historical Minimalism in art is not minimal marketing design. No material, spatial-installation or named-work reproduction claim. S37 remains unreviewed.

regions.label: Retained objects
regions.explanation: Count removes whole units; a staged reduction changes shape detail instead of recoloring it.

regions.label: Declared meaning
regions.explanation: The small original label is not a claim that less is universally better.

regions.label: Empty interval
regions.explanation: Blank field is a real spatial relationship, but not physical material presence.

movements.title: Maker, medium, point of view
movements.teaching: Read the Met S45 overview and curator Denise Murrell's audio-guide 681 transcript: Winold Reiss's Alain Leroy Locke (1925) is described as painting and drawing; Reiss illustrated Alain Locke's The New Negro. The overview relates modern Black life to Great Migration and multiple media. Now edit six wholly original neighborhood scenes and their point of view, not a racialized palette filter or a portrait replica.
movements.limits: Our fictional everyday-life sequence is not a named historical replica, participant testimony, community approval or one formal language for Black art. Named passage evidence is narrow; canonical S45/record statuses are not promoted. Original vector medium differs from the cited painting/drawing.

regions.label: Original fictional setting
regions.explanation: A door, desk and window locate a fictional narrative; they do not represent a racial style.

regions.label: Declared narrative voice
regions.explanation: Words identify an authored viewpoint rather than fabricating participant testimony.

regions.label: Maker/medium/source boundary
regions.explanation: A separate source note connects Winold Reiss, painting/drawing and The New Negro; the new vector scene is not that work.

contextEvidence.medium: Painting and drawing, as described by curator Denise Murrell for Alain Leroy Locke (1925)
contextEvidence.locator: Overview paragraphs 1–2; Audio Guide 681, Show Transcript, Denise Murrell paragraph
contextEvidence.limits: Named source body and transcript only; no artwork copied, rights clearance or canonical status promotion.
